[9] Two major distinctions of our discipline, among the engineering disciplines, is the unique focus of industrial and systems engineering on human factors and the quantification and systematic removal of uncertainty from production systems. A minor in Arabic Studies also helps to prepare students for careers in education, international development, non-profit agencies and NGOs, translating and interpreting, public relations and marketing, government service, international law, international business, engineering, and research. This minor is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences, who wishes to add an international dimension to their intellectual profile. A C or better is required for a course to be counted in the minor. [4]

The minor in architectural fabrication and product design provides opportunities for creativity while learning professional tools and techniques. You will gain a broad understanding of terminology, history, prototyping and professional practices. With this minor, there are specific credit hours that allow you to develop in your design experience through design seminars. [3]

An interdisciplinary and global approach is used to understand heritage conservation and its importance in the sustainable conservation of the built environment. The curriculum emphasizes an awareness of principles and theories that affect architectural heritage conservation. In addition, the minor enables students to explore technological advances critical to documenting and assessing the built environment. The Minor in Architectural Heritage Conservation can serve as a complement to several major fields of study and is open to all Texas A&M undergraduates. The structure of the minor encourages students to gain a broad understanding of the foundations of conservation before moving on to specialized areas of interest.
ScholarshipType: academic achievement, financial need, extracurricular activities, leadership and community service

Requirements: Applicants must have a 3.25 or better overall GPA and have completed less than 70 hours. [4] A 10-piece portfolio is also required for consideration. [4] To apply, students must email the Studio Art Minor Application PDF to the program director. [4, 5] A grade of C or better must be made in each course to be awarded the minor. [4, 5]
Department: College of Architecture, Department of Visualization
Description: Traditional art and digital courses help to broaden students' skill sets in analog and digital tools. Courses provide an understanding of tools and processes which can then be specialized through electives including painting, sculpting and time-based media. The 16-credit-hour minor provides a broad orientation to the visual arts. [4]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, and field-specific scholarships are available for undergraduate students.

Requirements: The Minor in Art and Architectural History is open to all Texas A&M undergraduates. [5] Applicants must have a 2.0 or better overall GPR to be considered for the program. [7] Students wishing to declare a minor should consult with advisors in their home college or school and in the Department of Architecture. [7] To be officially awarded the minor, a student must earn a grade of “C” or better in each course. [3] Students must also complete a minimum of 6 hours in residence at the 300-400 level. [5]
Description: The minor in art and architecture history provides undergraduate students with an interdisciplinary, global, and multicultural approach to understanding visual arts and the built environment. With an emphasis on awareness of diverse global cultures and historical traditions, you will gain skills of context, visual understanding and critical thinking. [4] This minor can serve as a complement to several major fields of study and is open to all Texas A&M undergraduates. [4]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, and other specific criteria

Requirements: To declare the Astrophysics minor, you must fill out the ASTP Minor Declaration Form and email it as a PDF file to advising@physics.tamu.edu. [8] Students are required to complete specific coursework with a grade of C or better to earn the minor. [11]
Description: The Minor in Astrophysics is designed for students interested in the mathematical foundation of astronomy. It is particularly relevant for those in engineering and physics who may require a fundamental understanding of the universe's physics in their future careers. The program also caters to students aiming for careers in fields that benefit from a technical knowledge of astronomy, such as science writing, scientific journalism, or science education. [7] The curriculum covers the origin, growth, and ultimate fate of the Universe, including physical laws on the largest scales, planets in the Solar System, exoplanets, massive black holes, and galaxies. [7] Students will develop technical skills and problem-solving abilities applicable in the modern high-technology world. [7] To complete the minor, students must satisfy requirements with a C or better in courses including PHYS 207/227, ASTR 314, ASTR 320, and 6 hours of ASTR courses from a selected list. [9]

Requirements: As long as you are a current undergraduate student at Texas A&M University you are eligible to pursue our minors. [3] Declaration of minor is made in the student's home college or major department. [3] Students seeking a minor must: Meet all minor course prerequisites, obtain a grade of 'C' or better in all minor courses, and complete the appropriate minor form to have approved and signed by an advisor in our department, you must schedule an advising appointment to have the form processed. [3]
Description: The Biochemistry minor provides a rigorous exploration of cellular processes at the molecular level, covering essential topics such as enzyme kinetics, metabolic pathways, and molecular interactions.

Requirements: To be eligible for the Minor in Biomedical Engineering, students must be admitted to a College of Engineering major and have a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0. [5] The application process requires completing the BMEN minor application and an essay of a maximum of 250 words explaining why the student wants a biomedical engineering minor. [5] Applicants must maintain a 2.0 GPA in minor courses and complete the courses listed for their selected track. [5] All tracks require the completion of MATH 308 (Differential Equations). [3] No more than 6 hours from the student's home department can be used to satisfy the minor's requirements. [3]
Concentration: ['Biomechanics Track', 'Cellular and Molecular Bioengineering Track', 'Imaging, Sensing and Digital Health track']
Description: The Department of Biomedical Engineering (BMEN) offers a minor to students in the College of Engineering who are interested in biomedical applications of engineering related to the fields of biomechanics, biomaterials and bioinstrumentation. [3] Eligible students must submit an application to be considered for and allowed to pursue a Minor in Biomedical Engineering. [3] The program requires students to select courses exclusively from one of the offered tracks. [3, 7] All tracks require the completion of math through Differential Equations (MATH 308), and students may use no more than 6 hours from their home department to satisfy minor requirements. [7]
MinimumGMATScore: Verbal Score of at least 77 on the new scale or 22 on the old scale (subject to departmental approval)
MinimumGreScore: Verbal Reasoning score of at least 146 (subject to departmental approval)

Description: The minor in business consists of six specific courses chosen to develop foundational knowledge in the basic aspects of business, including accounting, finance, management, marketing, and management information systems. [3] The courses listed below constitute the 18 hours required for a minor in business.

Students seeking a minor in chemistry must complete the Declaration of Minor in Chemistry form and have it approved by the undergraduate advisor in chemistry and their academic advisor. A minor in Chemistry should represent course work taken in the discipline beyond courses that might be used to satisfy core curriculum science requirements (8 credits). Therefore, though CHEM 119 or CHEM 107/CHEM 117 and CHEM 120 are prerequisites to all of the listed courses, they are not considered part of the minor program. The course work listed represents various sub- disciplines within the field of Chemistry and would give the student an overall knowledge base fitting a Minor in Chemistry. This is consistent with the statement on minors published by the American Chemical Society. [14]

This minor is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences, who wishes to add Chinese language proficiency and an international dimension to their intellectual profile. [12] The minor in Chinese is an academic program open to all students in the university. [10] The minor is interdisciplinary in nature and combines courses in Chinese language and culture with electives in Chinese studies, as well as a capstone project. [10] A minor in Chinese also helps to prepare students for careers in education, international development, non-profit agencies and NGOs, translating and interpreting, public relations and marketing, government service, international law, international business, engineering, global health, and research. [10] In addition, Chinese studies faculty offer study abroad programs in order to enrich student learning experiences and cultural knowledge while helping students attain higher proficiency in the language. [10] The capstone project allows students to integrate knowledge and skills about topics pertaining to Chinese language, culture, history, geography, etc. that they have gained through their coursework, including any study abroad experience in China. [11] Students will consult with the faculty in Chinese and meet regularly with a faculty advisor to complete an independent research project about a topic of their interest pertaining to China. [11]

The interdisciplinary classical studies minor combines courses in Greek or Latin language with electives in multiple disciplines and is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences. [6] The focus on the history, beliefs, and material culture of ancient Greek and Roman civilization helps students to see how fundamental concepts of Western Civilization first arose in Classical Antiquity, and is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences. [10] A minor in Classics also helps to prepare students for careers in education, international development, non-profit agencies and NGOs, translating and interpreting, public relations and marketing, government service, international law, international business, engineering, global health, and research. [10]

The minor in Climate Change aims to provide an overview of how the climate system works from an earth systems sciences perspective and how humans and the environment interact within it. Climate change is one of the most pressing issues of our time. It will impact every aspect of our lives, and unless our economies take aggressive action to reduce emissions, today's students will live through climate change unprecedented in modern human history. The minor in Climate Change draws on multiple courses exploring the science of climate change as well as the multitude of impacts ranging from farming and food production, water availability, ocean acidification to the potential of sustainable energy to replace fossil fuels, as well as the policy decisions governments are making. Students learn about climate change and how to understand and forecast its potential impacts from varied disciplinary and interdisciplinary perspectives, while getting a firm grounding in the basic physical, ecological and social sciences. [5, 12]

This minor is designed for students who are pursuing coaching in various settings, such as public and private schools, club sports, and youth sport leagues. This program may also be useful for those who plan to work in the fitness industry. [4] Admission to this minor is by application only and requires completion of BIOL 111. [4] Students should consult with a College of Education and Human Development academic advisor for admission requirements and application. [4] Students should allow a minimum of three semesters to complete this minor. [4, 5] Students must make a grade of C or better in all courses. [4]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Field of Study, Demographic, Community Service

Concentration: Comparative Cultural Studies – International
Description.1: The minor in Comparative Cultural Studies – International focuses on how culture and politics affect societies across the world. [4] The program's strong interdisciplinary approach in the humanities and social sciences gives students the skills and competencies they need to address complex and critical global issues. [4] The minor provides students with tools to better understand cultural perspectives from around the world. [4] The comparative and transnational focus encourages students to learn about other cultures and social systems, to reflect back on their own societies, and to discover how they want to position themselves as globally engaged citizens. [4] The coursework gives students the opportunity to gain expertise in areas or cultures outside of the United States and allows them to develop comparative and international perspectives valued by public and private employers. [4] The courses recommended for the minor examine such issues as media, power, politics, literature, film, performance, globalization, international development, and global public health. [4]

Description: The minor in computer science provides the student with an introduction to the fundamentals of this area of study. The minor, available to students in all majors (except for CPSC, COMP, CPEN, CECN and CEEN - see Additional Notes below), focuses on developing a basic foundation in computing, including components of programming, data structures and algorithm analysis, and computer architecture.
MaxFails: A student is placed on scholastic probation if their semester or cumulative GPA falls below 2.00. Failure to meet the terms of probation can lead to dismissal from the major or suspension from the university.

Description: The Department of Educational Psychology offers a minor in Creative Studies. This minor provides students with increased knowledge and innovative thinking that can be applied to one's professional and personal life. [3] Students interested in declaring the Creative Studies minor may seek additional information from the EPSY Undergraduate Advisor in Harrington Tower.

The Cybersecurity Minor provides a basic understanding of programming and a firmly grounded understanding of cybersecurity, including cyber ethics. [3] Students can specialize in the area of cybersecurity that is most closely aligned with their interests and degree plans. [3]

Concentration: Dance Performance Minor
Description: This minor allows students to deepen their technical training and focuses on the performance of concert dance. Students who want to pursue a professional career in dance will benefit from this minor, as will students who want to improve their overall dance training. The minor includes interdisciplinary opportunities by examining the role of technology in dance through our Performance in Virtual and Augmented Reality course. The physical nature of dance is also emphasized, including a conditioning course to maximize performance and minimize injury. Additional courses include dance technique classes in ballet, modern, jazz, hip-hop, tap, improvisation and partnering. All students seeking a Dance Performance minor must be admitted through an application and audition process administered by the Texas A&M Dance faculty. [3] Note: Texas A&M also offers a 'Choreography - Minor'. [15]
Accredidation: Texas A&M University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees. [4] No specific accreditation for the minor in dance was found on the official website.

Description: A minimum grade point average of 2.75 is required for entering the minor. Prerequisite coursework includes the calculus sequence, MATH 308, and PHYS 207 or equivalents. Students must make a grade of "C" or better in all courses. All courses must be taken at Texas A&M University; no transfer work will be accepted. Students majoring in Computer Engineering will not be permitted to minor in Electrical Engineering since the coursework prescribed for the minor is required coursework for the Computer Engineering degree. [8]

An English minor teaches students to communicate clearly and effectively, learn how to critically read and examine complex texts, build effective arguments, and recognize other points of view. [9] Through an English minor, you'll learn how to: Communicate clearly and effectively, Critically read and examine complex texts, Build effective arguments, Recognize other points of view. [8] You will have the opportunity to take courses in: Creative writing, Rhetoric, Science fiction and fantasy, African-American and Latinx literature, Gender and sexuality studies, and Digital humanities. [8]

The Minor in Environmental Geosciences offers a rigorous, interdisciplinary education in issues associated with environmental policy. The coursework covers all geosciences disciplines, focusing on atmospheric sciences and air quality, resources and the environment, oceanography and marine pollution, environmental geology, and climate change. [2] This program is designed to prepare students for careers in industry, environmental and engineering consulting firms, non-governmental organizations, and governmental regulatory agencies. [2]

ScholarshipType: University scholarships are awarded on the basis of academic merit, leadership/participation, and financial need or any combination of these items. [16]

Description: The Minor in Film Studies trains students to apply film criticism as well as to participate in the production of short films. The program includes six core courses, three of which focus on film analysis. The developing ideas and applying them to script formats leads to the acquisition of technical skills required for filmmaking. Two electives are devoted to Arab Cinema on one hand and to the genre of animation film on the other.

The minor in Financial Planning prepares students for leadership roles in a rapidly growing profession. Financial planners advise their clients about financial decisions, including investments, insurance, taxes, retirement, estate planning, and budgeting. The goal of a financial planner is to help households bring confidence and peace of mind through the establishment of a financial plan to meet their life goals.
Accredidation: All programs are registered with the Certified Financial Planner (CFP) Board of Standards. [13, 14]

Description: The Department of Global Languages and Cultures offers a minor in French. This program is designed for students to gain language and/or cultural proficiency in French. The minor is considered a valuable complement to the academic portfolio for students in various fields who wish to add an international dimension to their intellectual profile. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Game Design and Development
Department: The minor is offered through a cooperation between the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the Department of Visualization. The Department of Visualization is part of the College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts.
Fees: A specific tuition fee for the minor is not listed. The cost is part of the student's overall tuition based on their specific circumstances. The university's tuition calculator can be used for an estimate.
Description: The minor in Game Design and Development offers students the opportunity to develop knowledge and skill associated with the aesthetic and technical aspects of interactive media. In collaboration with other students, you will learn core competencies as well as engage in creative problem solving. The 16-credit-hour minor provides a foundation in the principles of game design and software development. The curriculum includes art, design, programming, media literacy, and video game production.
CostPerCredit: A specific cost per credit for the minor is not provided. Undergraduate tuition is assessed based on factors such as the student's college, residency, and total credit hours.
ScholarshipAmount: The College of Performance, Visualization and Fine Arts offers scholarships with awards ranging from $500 to $2,000. [11]
ScholarshipType: The College of Performance, Visualization and Fine Arts offers various scholarships, including College Level and Program Level Scholarships, Study Abroad/Exchange Scholarships, and Research Assistance Scholarships. [11] The Department of Computer Science and Engineering also provides scholarship opportunities.

Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: This program delves deep into the fascinating realm of heredity, encompassing principles of inheritance, genetic variation, and the molecular mechanisms that govern gene expression. [6] The Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics offers a minor in Genetics. [6] Students seeking a minor must complete a minor form and have it approved and signed by the BICH/GENE undergraduate advisor and their major academic advisor. [6] Students are required to meet all minor course prerequisites. [6]

Geography coursework for this minor integrates physical sciences, social sciences, and the humanities. [5] Geography explores the relationships between people and their environment, which vary from place to place across the Earth. [5] Geographers compare and quantify the drivers of the variable and changing characteristics of Earth's systems, which have been transformed into human habitat and are thus undergoing change. [5, 10]

This minor combines courses in German language and culture and is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences who wishes to add linguistic proficiency in German and an international dimension to their intellectual profile. [10]

A history minor adds depth to any course of study at Texas A&M. Students in the sciences and engineering, for example, pursue the minor to sharpen writing and critical thinking skills. Students from all majors are welcome! [3]

Requirements: Students must have a 2.0 cumulative GPA to be admitted into the program. [6] To declare the minor, students should meet with their departmental academic advisor to discuss minor options and how the courses may apply to their specific degree plan. The advisor can then "apply" the minor request to the student's degree plan record. [6] A grade of "C" or better is required in all courses for the minor. [8]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: The Department of Horticultural Science at Texas A&M University offers an undergraduate minor in Horticulture, which provides students with a concentration of courses that focus on areas of horticulture and floriculture. [3] These may range from a broad-based, comparative perspective to a narrower application within the field. [3] Students may choose such diverse topics as fruit and vegetable production, enology, greenhouse and nursery management, floral and landscape design, science and biotechnology, urban and environmental horticulture, and much more. [3] Earning a minor in HORT provides students with the skills required to have a basic working knowledge of the field of Horticulture. [3] The program covers topics like crop production, enology, greenhouse management, floral design, and biotechnology, providing students with essential horticultural skills. [5, 11] The program is comprised of 18 credit hours of HORT courses, with a minimum of 9 at the 300-400 level. [3] HORT 201 is required of all HORT minors. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in International and Comparative Politics
Description: The Minor in Comparative Politics provides students with opportunities to explore the diverse political systems worldwide, examining governance structures, political behavior and institutions across different nations to understand comparative political dynamics and their impact on global affairs. [1]

This minor combines courses in Italian language and culture, and is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences, who wishes to add linguistic proficiency in Italian and an international dimension to their intellectual profile. [6]

The minor in Japanese is an academic program open to all students in the university. [4, 11] The minor is interdisciplinary in nature and combines courses in Japanese language and culture with electives in Japanese studies, as well as a capstone project. [4, 11] This minor is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences, who wishes to add linguistic proficiency in Japanese and an international dimension to their intellectual profile. [4, 11] A minor in Japanese also helps to prepare students for careers in education, international development, non-profit agencies and NGOs, translating and interpreting, public relations and marketing, government service, international law, international business, engineering, global health, and research. [11] A capstone project, completed in an approved upper-division Japanese course, is required for all students in the minor during their final year. [10, 11] This project allows students to integrate knowledge on topics related to Japanese language, culture, history, and geography. [10, 11]

The Department of Communication and Journalism offers a minor in Journalism, which complements any major and provides essential tools for students who aspire to share ethically sourced and fact-checked reports with the public. The Journalism minor offers foundational skills in reporting, including interviewing techniques and online research, as well as writing skills for deadline news stories, longer analytical pieces, and feature articles. Students also explore multi-media journalism and have the opportunity to take specialized advanced writing courses.

The landscape architecture minor is designed to introduce the content and contributions of the field to students outside the professional program. The minor is an eighteen-hour curriculum that includes nice [sic] credit hours of core courses and nine credit hours of elective courses. The core nine credit hour curriculum introduces basic knowledge in design thinking, the history of landscape architecture and urbanism. The elective courses include courses that explore different trajectories within the area of landscape architecture including cultural landscapes, representation, social justice, plants and ecology and urbanism.

This program provides students with formal instruction in leadership theory and the application of concepts necessary to be successful leaders in future careers. The Leadership (LDAG) curriculum prepares students to be effective industry, community, and organizational leaders. Students explore leadership roles in their future contexts, develop an awareness of personal leadership characteristics, and apply leadership theories and models for future professional experiences. The coursework includes foundational leadership concepts and advanced leadership concepts.

ProgramName: Minor in Materials Science and Engineering
Description: The Materials Science and Engineering minor program is designed to provide a strong materials science educational program for undergraduate science and engineering majors and to integrate a materials focus into their undergraduate training. [7, 5] This program is intended for students interested in enriching their major undergraduate program of study to incorporate a fundamental understanding of materials processing and structure–property relationships to complement their primary degree. [11, 5] Students will have the flexibility to select relevant coursework to customize this program of study to best suit their intended area of focus through consultation with an MSEN faculty advisor. [7, 5] All students are required to have completed an introductory materials science and engineering prerequisite course before applying for the minor. The prerequisite course does not apply to the minor. [7] Completion of the minor will be recorded on the student's university transcript. [7]

Requirements: To obtain a minor in Meteorology, students must complete a minimum of 16 credit hours in Atmospheric Sciences (ATMO) or upper-division Geosciences (GEOS) courses, with no more than 6 hours from GEOS. [4] A minimum of 9 of the 16 hours must be at the 300-level or above, including at least three 400-level hours. [4] A minimum GPA of 2.0 must be maintained for the minor. [5, 6] Prerequisites for the minor include either two semesters of calculus or two semesters of chemistry. [4] Students interested in declaring the minor should contact the department's academic advisor to set up an appointment. [4]
Description: The minor in Meteorology begins with a broad survey of the atmospheric sciences and associated weather analysis. It is then followed by a more detailed introduction to at least one subdiscipline of the atmospheric sciences, such as atmospheric chemistry, dynamics, computer applications, or severe weather. The minor also introduces students to related Earth systems topics, such as oceanography, Earth-surface processes, or atmosphere-biosphere interactions. Students interested in pursuing the minor are encouraged to meet with the department's academic advisor to identify appropriate courses. [7]

Requirements: To declare a minor, students must meet with an academic advisor. [9] The music minor requires 15-18 hours of coursework, with at least six of those hours being at the 300-400 level and completed in residence. [9] Students are required to earn a grade of 'C' or better in all courses for the minor and maintain a minimum GPA of 2.7. [3]
Description: The Minor in Music gives students the opportunity to pursue musical interests while developing skills and exploring the history and context of music. This minor prepares students to a develop fundamental a fundamental understanding of music through introductory music theory, musicianship, and music history. Through individual instruction or group performance, students will have opportunities to perform, to develop skills on their preferred instrument(s), and/or to learn new instruments and styles. Students can choose from a variety of electives, tailoring their course of instruction to their own needs and interests. This flexible minor allows students to complement their major field of study and prepares them for post-graduation pathways that integrate music into their personal and professional life. [3, 4]

Requirements: To declare a minor in music technology, current students must fill out and submit an application form. [7] Minors must be formally declared with an advisor to be included on the student's record. [7]
Description: This program focuses on preparing students to think about music and sound in new ways. [9] Beyond clean audio editing and using off-the-shelf products in conventional ways, the minor in music technology guides students in exploring novel approaches to musical expression through technology-based live performance, fixed media art, installation art and interdisciplinary creative work. [3] Required courses provide a broad range of experiences in composing with sound; digital audio editing and signal processing; recording techniques; and merging music with other disciplines in novel and thought-provoking ways. [3] Throughout the minor, students will build a portfolio of creative work demonstrating their experience and unique voices as 21st century musicians ready to make the most creative use of emerging technologies. [3]

A minor in Neuroscience is considered an interdisciplinary minor with course selections in Biology, Psychology, Philosophy and Veterinary Integrative Biosciences. Please be aware that each course selection may have prerequisite requirements that must be met. The coursework listed represents various sub-disciplines within the field of Neuroscience and would give the student an overall knowledge base fitting a minor in Neuroscience. [9]

Oceanography is an interdisciplinary science that focuses on the oceans, their contents and their boundaries. [5, 9, 11] The Department of Oceanography offers a 15-credit-hour minor in Oceanography for undergraduate students. [3] Students may take any combination of Oceanography courses including research credit hours with an individual faculty member. [3] Qualified undergraduate students may participate in a 15-credit minor in Oceanography. [9] The following majors may not minor in Oceanography: BA Ocean Studies, BS Oceanography, BS Marine Science, and all combination Master of Ocean Science and Technology programs. [9]

ProgramName: Minor in Park and Natural Resource Management
Department: Department of Rangeland, Wildlife and Fisheries Management
Description: This program focuses on integrating concepts of bio-environmental sciences, social and behavioral sciences, and policy and administrative decision-making to equip future land managers and related professionals with the background and skills necessary for the management of natural and cultural resources associated with conserving parks and other protected areas. [4] The minor in Park and Natural Resource Management is offered from the Department of Rangeland, Wildlife and Fisheries Management (RWFM) for undergraduate majors to further refine their studies. [4, 5] This minor is ideal for students interested in careers in recreation, park, and tourism fields, including those offered by state and federal agencies, private enterprises, non-profit organizations, youth camps, and environmental education programs. [4]

The Department of Philosophy offers a minor in Philosophy, which requires 15 credit hours of coursework. At least 9 of these hours must be in upper-division courses. Students can choose any five philosophy courses to fulfill the minor, with the recommendation that at least three of them are at the 300-level or higher.

The Minor in Physics will develop analytical thinking and quantitative problem-solving skills that students can apply in any field. It will also give students the basic knowledge to make informed decisions, advise, instruct, or administrate in our modern science- and technology-dominated world.

Department: Department of Soil and Crop Sciences
Description: TThe minor in plant breeding prepares agricultural majors for a career in nation's variety development industry and exposes the student to an academic discipline that could lead to the pursuit of advanced degrees and a career in the field of plant breeding. The Department of Soil and Crop Sciences offers a Minor in Plant Breeding. Plant breeders develop new varieties that are the cornerstone of modern agriculture and improve the genetic basis of improved yield, quality, and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses affecting or nation's food, feed, fiber, greenspace, shelter, and bioenergy plants. The Plant Breeding minor offers the opportunity for students to explore their interest in applied biological sciences in the areas of plant breeding, crop improvement, crop biotechnology, and genetics.

ScholarshipType: Merit-Based, Need-Based, Demographic, Field of Study, Community Service

Description: The Department of Political Science at Texas A&M University, College Station, does not offer a single, general 'Minor in Political Science'. Instead, it provides seven distinct minors for students. [4] These minors are: Political Science – Legal Foundations (LFND), Political Science – Comparative Politics (CMPL), Political Science – American Politics & Policy (AMPP), Political Science – International Relations (INRL), Political Science – Political Theory (PTHE), Political Science – Political Data & Research (PDRS), and Political Science – Race, Ethnic, & Gender Politics (REGP). [4] Each has its own specific focus and requirements. To declare one of these minors, students are required to complete an application. [4]

A minor in psychology can be a valuable supplement to education in almost any field. Students select from a variety of courses that enhance their understanding of animal or human behavior, the skills to intervene to change behavior and to create environments that support healthy behavior, and critical thinking skills related to asking and answering questions about human behavior. This knowledge prepares students to pursue a variety of careers where interacting with people is a central job component. [4] This minor is available for non-psychological and brain science majors. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Race and Ethnic Studies
Requirements: All freshman applicants must complete a Self-reported Transcript and Academic Record System (STARS) except for GED graduates. The STARS Record replaces the high school transcripts used by the Office of Admissions during the initial admission process in most cases. [24] Applicants create the STARS Record using their official high school transcript, listing courses and associated grades that have been completed or will be completed for high school and/or college credit. [24] An essay is also required. [25] For graduate admissions, applicants must hold a bachelor's degree or its equivalent. [10] Most graduate information is specific to different colleges and programs, so applicants should reach out to their department for specific admissions information like deadlines and required documents. [10]

A minor in Religious Studies consists of 15 hours. A grade of C or better is required in all courses. At least 9 semester credit hours must be 300-400 level courses. An option of up to 6 semester credit hours in Arabic, Latin, and Greek at the 200 or 300 level is available. [13, 14, 15] To add the Religious Studies minor, students must complete an application, which can be found on the department's webpage. [14]
Description: The Religious Studies Minor offers students the opportunity to better understand how religion addresses core concerns about human existence across cultures. [10] Students who minor in Religious Studies select from a range of courses that match their interests and goals from a variety of disciplines in the College of Arts and Sciences. [11] You'll gain perspective on the complexity of religious thought and practices in world cultures. [4] This minor will help you understand the significance of religion at individual, interpersonal, social and cultural level. [4] Students have the opportunity to study specific religious traditions, to approach religion through the study of rituals, symbols, and literature, and to examine religion as a human phenomenon situated in culture and history. [4, 11] The skills you will learn through the study of religion as a human endeavor provide an intellectual foundation for any future career, emphasizing critical thinking, problem solving, cultural understanding, and communication. [4]
CostPerCredit: Texas A&M University does not have a fixed cost per credit hour as some fees and tuition are flat rates. [21] A tuition calculator is provided on the university's Student Business Services website to estimate costs. [9]
MinGPA: Grade of C or better in all courses required for the minor. [10]
ScholarshipAmount: Awards range in value from $500 to $7,500 for continuing students. [6]
ScholarshipType: Several schools/colleges and departments at Texas A&M award scholarships to students based on academic record, service, activities, and demonstrated leadership. [6]

Requirements: The minor in Russian is an academic program open to all students in the university. [3, 7] To declare the minor, students must have completed RUSS 101 and RUSS 102 as prerequisites and be enrolled in or have completed RUSS 201. [6] The minor must be declared before a student completes 90 credit hours. [6] A total of 18 semester credit hours are required, and students must earn a grade of C or better in all minor coursework. [3, 6]
Description: The minor combines courses in Russian language and culture, and is a valuable complement to the academic portfolio of any student majoring in the humanities, social sciences, or natural sciences, who wishes to add linguistic proficiency in Russian and an international dimension to their intellectual profile. [9, 12] The minor in Russian is an academic program open to all students in the university. [11, 12] A minor in Russian also helps to prepare students for careers in education, international development, non-profit agencies and NGOs, translating and interpreting, public relations and marketing, government service, international law, international business, engineering, global health, and research. [12] In addition, Russian studies faculty offer study abroad programs in order to enrich student learning experiences and cultural knowledge while helping students attain higher proficiency in the language. [12]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available.

Requirements: Information regarding specific application requirements for the Minor in Safety Engineering, such as a formal application, is not available on the Texas A&M University, College Station website. The general process for minors at the university involves meeting with an academic advisor to declare the minor after fulfilling any prerequisite courses.
Description: The Artie McFerrin Department of Chemical Engineering offers a minor in Safety Engineering. [3] The Mary Kay O'Connor Process Safety Center (MKOPSC) at Texas A&M University has played a significant role in incorporating process safety into the chemical engineering curriculum. [5] The center offers a safety certificate to all engineering disciplines at the graduate and undergraduate level as a minor in safety engineering, provided coursework requirements are met. [5] The Dr. Sam Mannan Endowed Scholarship is available for students pursuing an undergraduate degree in Chemical Engineering with a minor in Safety Engineering. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Social and Behavioral Sciences

Requirements: To declare a minor in Sociology, students must meet several requirements. You must be a current student at Texas A&M University with grades posted for at least one completed semester. [3] An overall GPA of 2.0 or higher is necessary, along with having completed at least one sociology course with a GPA of 2.0 or better in all sociology coursework. [3] Additionally, students should not have completed more than 90 credit hours. [3] The minor itself consists of 15 hours of coursework, and a grade of C or better is required for all courses. [7] Of these 15 hours, at least 9 must be at the 300- or 400-level. [7]
Description: A minor in sociology can be a valuable complement to a degree in almost any field of study. You will select from a variety of courses to enhance the ability to live and work effectively in a global society. You'll gain a better understanding of social and cultural trends, inequalities, organizational behavior and community and world events. Learn to address real world problems by: Developing realistic and equitable solutions. Thinking critically about complex problems and ideas. Engaging in communication processes with varied audiences. [3]

Requirements: To declare a minor in Spanish, students must complete the prerequisite courses: SPAN 101, SPAN 102, SPAN 201, and SPAN 202. [10] The minor must be declared before a student completes 90 credit hours. [10] The minor requires a total of 18 credit hours, and at least 9 of these must be taken at Texas A&M. [9] A grade of 'C' or better is necessary for a course to be counted towards the minor. [9, 10]
Concentration: ['Business-Law and Law Enforcement', 'Culture, Art, and Cinema', 'Heritage Language', 'Linguistics', 'Literature']
Description: The Spanish minor allows students with other majors to work on their linguistic skills while they gain Hispanic cultural competency. A great way to complement coursework in many other majors, including those in science, health, and business, this minor focuses on language-based coursework that will serve as an asset upon entering the job market after graduation. A minor in Spanish also helps to prepare students for careers in education, international development, non-profit agencies and NGOs, translating and interpreting, public relations and marketing, government service, international law, international business, engineering, and research. [5] The themes are recommendations and may be combined with other themes or other elective courses. Completion of theme courses does not in itself confer a minor.

Requirements: You must be a current student at Texas A&M University to declare this minor. Please contact your major advisor to declare a minor in Howdy. [8]
Description: Our Sport Management minor is designed for students who want an introduction to working with sport organizations. All of the courses for the minor in Sport Management are available online. Two of the minor courses will also meet international and cultural requirements for core curriculum. You must be a current student at Texas A&M University to declare this minor. Please contact your major advisor to declare a minor in Howdy.

Requirements: To declare a minor in Statistics, students must add the courses they plan to take for the Statistics minor to their Undergraduate Degree Planner and email undergraduate@stat.tamu.edu (and include your UIN) to request approval for the minor. [3, 4] It is encouraged that students are registered in or have completed STAT 211 before declaring. [3, 4] Students must make a grade of C or better in all courses for the minor. [5]
Description: Statistics is the science of collecting and analyzing data for the purpose of making decisions in the presence of uncertainty. Multidisciplinary application areas vary widely and include health and medicine, business, engineering, physical sciences, environmental studies, and government. The statistics minor provides training in theoretical, applied and computational statistics with a two-semester sequence in statistical methods (STAT 211/STAT 212) and a broad selection of upper-level elective classes. Depending on the electives selected, a student completing this program will be prepared to conduct statistical analysis in their professional work or to continue graduate study in fields involving statistical analysis. [3]

Requirements: Student applying for a minor in Sustainable Architecture and Planning must have a 2.0 or better overall GPR. [3] Students must receive signed approval from the Department of Architecture Undergraduate Advisor for the minor. After approval, the application is completed in the student's home college or major department. [3] Students must make a grade of "C" or better in all courses. [5]
Fees: $12,995 for in-state and $40,124 for out-of-state students. [7]
Description: The Minor in Sustainable Architecture and Planning (SARP) provides undergraduate students with a multidisciplinary approach to an understanding of sustainability of the built environment. [7] The curriculum emphasizes an awareness of responsible practices on a variety of scales impacting the built environment: buildings, communities, architectural systems, global resource management, and social equity. [7, 6] Students will become aware of responsible architectural design and develop critical thinking skills to address the multifaceted issues facing the profession today. [7, 6] The Minor in Sustainable Architecture and Planning can serve as a complement to several major fields of study and is open to all Texas A&M undergraduates. [7, 6] The structure of the minor encourages students to gain a broad understanding before advancing to specialized areas of interest. [7, 6]

Requirements: A minor in Theatre requires a minimum of 16 hours in theatre courses. It must include 10 hours of core courses, plus a minimum of 6 hours of elective courses. [3] A minimum of one elective course must be from the History/Criticism category and one course must be from the Production/Performance category. [3] 6 hours of the 16 total hours in the minor must be in classes at the 300 level higher. [3] Students must officially declare the minor with their college. [3] The minor declaration process varies from college to college and it is up to the student to discuss with their academic advisor what their particular process entails. [3] Upon completion of meeting with their advisor students may then fill out a Statement of Intent. [3]
Description: The Minor in Theatre offers students a comprehensive overview of the study of theatre, including both academic (history and criticism) and production (acting, design and technology) courses. [3] The purpose is to expose undergraduate students to the field by reinforcing the integrated nature of theatre as a scholarly and aesthetic pursuit. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Urban and Regional Planning
Requirements: Applicants must have a 2.0 or better overall GPR to be considered for the program. Students wishing to declare a minor in urban planning should consult with advisors in their home college or school and in the Department of Landscape Architecture and Urban Planning.
Description: As our urban environment continues to grow, the minor in urban planning will prepare you to manage increasingly complex areas. Our program combines multi-disciplinary study with critical thinking skills to solve challenges in communities, cities, and the natural environment. [1]

Requirements:
Texas A&M University does not offer a specific minor program titled 'Minor in Viticulture and Enology'. However, it does offer a 'Horticultural Minor' where students can choose to focus on enology. [2] To be admitted into the Horticultural Minor, a student must have a cumulative GPA of 2.0. [2] Students are not required to meet with an advisor to declare the minor. [2] The process involves meeting with their departmental academic advisor to have the minor added to their degree plan. [2]

Additionally, Texas A&M offers a 'Certificate in Viticulture and Enology'. [9] To be admitted to this certificate program, students must be enrolled in a degree program at Texas A&M, have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0, and submit an application. [9]

Description: The Viticulture and Enology Certificate, offered by the Department of Horticultural Sciences, contains 15 hours of concentrated study in the areas of viticulture, pre- and post-fermentation winemaking processes, wine etiquette, and sensory evaluation. [5] The certificate is designed to provide a knowledge base to those individuals who have an interest in pursuing a career that involves the wine industry. [5] The certificate is open to all majors, but students should consult with their academic advisor prior to submitting a Viticulture and Enology Certificate program application. [5]

D. students) must be from outside the student's major department. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Women's and Gender Studies
Requirements: Students must make a grade of C or better in all courses. [8] At least 3 credits must be at the 300-400 level. [8]
Description: Students with this minor receive training in both humanities and social sciences approaches and are required to complete coursework that focuses on material beyond dominant U.S. culture; core courses have both theoretical and applied focuses. [3]

Requirements: Students must make a grade of C or better in all courses. [2] Any student interested in pursuing a minor through the Department of Agricultural Leadership, Education, and Communications should consult with their academic advisor. [1] The minor application follows the same dates as the Change of Curriculum application. [1]
Department: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Description: This program focuses on programs and services that contribute to the development of young people's personal, physical, social and educational abilities. The Department of Agricultural Leadership, Education and Communications offers a minor in Youth Development as a supplement to other majors. Youth workers are program developers, leaders and managers who need to be able to work with youth, families, organizations and communities. Coursework in this option focuses on positive youth development, program planning and evaluation, methods for working with young people, and societal factors that both contribute to and inhibit the development of young people.
ScholarshipAmount: $4,000/year for the Dean's Excellence Scholarship.
ScholarshipType: Scholarships are awarded based on academic accomplishments, financial need, and leadership potential. [7, 10]
